stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting it is a contemporary LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The tags confirm its relevance to the broader transformer and Llama ecosystem in AI.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when running with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
Model output quality has also been enhanced alongside the speed and efficiency gains.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM execution tools.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated support for MLX.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized performance.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging apps.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data privacy by running entirely on the user's device.
This represents a trend toward decentralized, on-device AI applications.

stories.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
stories.author: Simon Suo
bullet_points: Introduces ExtractBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for schema-guided document extraction in enterprise settings.
It is notable for being the first benchmark to evaluate multiple critical metrics simultaneously: value accuracy, record completeness, grounding, and measured cost.
The benchmark is substantial, comprising 4,869 pages across 370 different enterprise documents.

stories.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
stories.author: Zhichao Cao
bullet_points: TokTier addresses an inefficiency in LLM serving where front ends re-tokenize full requests instead of leveraging cached KV state.
The problem is highlighted by agentic workflows, where appending small tool results to long transcripts causes token boundary issues, hindering state reuse.
Empirical data shows that while most calls append small amounts of data, session rebuilding with large contexts remains a significant bottleneck.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp enhances model support across a broader range of hardware.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agentic workflows.

stories.title: Is paying artists enough to convince them to embrace AI?
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Generative AI models are being trained on artists' work without explicit permission.
Artists view this practice as theft, leading to significant ethical and legal disputes.
The debate pits artists' rights against the perceived necessity of data for AI technology evolution.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly reconsidering its licensing agreement with Google.
The uncertainty is linked to Reddit's stock performance and CEO skepticism regarding Google's AI Overviews.
This highlights ongoing tension and valuation debates surrounding major AI integrations between tech giants.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip for enhanced security.
The chip's design allows hackers to inspect the badge's contents.
The badge retains functionality even after the Defcon event, posing a persistent security risk.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is planning to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification requirements.
This change allows developers in countries like Cuba or Iran to continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy shift is expected to negatively impact developers operating in these sanctioned regions.

stories.title: AgentHPOBench: A Benchmark For Evaluating LLM Agents as Sequential Hyperparameter Optimizers
stories.author: Xuanjing Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AgentHPOBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating LLM agents.
The benchmark focuses on assessing agents' ability to act as sequential hyperparameter optimizers, a critical capability for autonomous scientific agents.
It addresses a gap in existing benchmarks that typically only test static code generation or final answer correctness, not iterative experimental decision-making.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically the compounding errors of standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research focuses on representational tradeoffs to enhance agent learning from expert demonstrations, relevant to robotics and LLM training.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI models to infer dyadic familiarity (stranger vs. familiar) from short social interactions.
The benchmark evaluates models across multimodal inputs (text, audio, video) by comparing them against human panels.
The research compares 26 models from seven different companies, focusing on non-verbal cues in ice-breaker conversations.

stories.title: TraceViT: Grounded Trace Supervision for Visual Abstract Reasoning
stories.author: Wei Hua
bullet_points: TraceViT is a new looped visual reasoner designed to improve performance on the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC).
The core innovation is introducing 'Grounded Trace Supervision,' which constrains the intermediate refinement steps of the model, not just the final output.
This addresses a limitation in conventional training methods for visual reasoners, allowing for step-by-step adherence to the inferred transformation.

stories.title: Sign compression for Muon: SignMuon, MuonSign, and the Limits of Error Feedback
stories.author: Alexey Kravatskiy
bullet_points: Introduces SignMuon, a new method to compress the Muon update to one bit per parameter for low-communication optimization.
SignMuon demonstrates practical superiority over SignSGD in performance benchmarks.
The research highlights a theoretical limitation where signing the gradient before the LMO causes ascent on linear functions, which the authors address with variations like MuonUSign and MuonSign.

stories.title: GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning
stories.author: Lutz Lampe
bullet_points: Addresses energy and resource constraints when deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices at the wireless edge.
Proposes a Green Quantized Federated Split Learning (GQ-FSL) framework to improve efficiency.
Mitigates overheads associated with traditional Federated Split Learning (FSL) by reducing data exchange energy consumption.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically compounding errors in standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research focuses on representational tradeoffs as a method to enhance the robustness of imitation learning algorithms.

stories.title: A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient
stories.author: Luis F. Lago-Fernández
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for trustworthy Explainable AI (XAI) in high-risk domains.
Proposes a new model-agnostic metric, the EPC score, to quantify explanation quality.
Focuses on balancing explanation fidelity with human-centered understanding, a current research challenge.

stories.title: QASP: Query-Adaptive Robust Vector Search Policy
stories.author: Andy Warfield
bullet_points: Addresses the core challenge in vector search: balancing high recall with low computational cost.
Introduces QASP, a Query-Adaptive robust vector Search Policy, to mitigate performance variance across different queries.
QASP uses a single upfront supervised regression to predict the full recall progression curve for any given query.

stories.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
stories.author: Adam Sobey
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) where shared LoRA adapters cause interference when training LLMs on diverse tasks.
Proposes a new optimization method to overcome the issues of poor transfer and catastrophic forgetting in multi-policy LLM training.
Moves beyond simply increasing adapter capacity or composing adapters by introducing a novel approach to task sequencing and optimization.

stories.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Xipeng Qiu
bullet_points: The paper introduces WCM, a World Critic Model, to address limitations in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
Existing critic-based RL methods struggle with partially observable robot control because they rely on single-frame observations or latent states.
WCM aims to overcome the exponential complexity associated with naively incorporating full observation history into the critic.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark designed to test the ability to infer dyadic familiarity (strangers vs. acquaintances) from short conversational clips.
The benchmark evaluates multimodal LLMs (text, audio, video) against human panels using 96 balanced dyads.
Focuses on behavioral cues in social interactions, highlighting that context and manner of interaction are as important as explicit language.

stories.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
stories.author: Shuo Shang
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for efficient long-context inference by tackling KV cache compression.
Existing compression methods either permanently discard information (eviction) or risk perturbing retained data (merging-based alternatives).
The proposed method, ResKV, formulates omitted attention contributions as residual statistics to allow for more accurate reconstruction.

stories.title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
stories.author: Simon Pietro Romano
bullet_points: Introduces ARB, a new benchmark dataset designed to evaluate AI-text detectors.
Addresses a gap in current research by testing detectors against human text rewritten by LLMs, rather than just direct LLM output.
The dataset is built from 1,800 human source texts, focusing on how rewriting affects detection accuracy.

stories.title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?
stories.author: Xining Xun
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that interventional data is always sufficient to teach causal reasoning in Language Models (LMs).
Testing in synthetic environments, the study found that increasing interventional samples does not guarantee improved causal direction.
Specifically, in scenarios like Simpson's paradox, the model's causal response magnitude increases monotonically despite the presence of interventional data.

stories.title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization
stories.author: Emmanuele Chersoni
bullet_points: Investigates the critical issue of memory utilization in personalized Large Language Model (LLM) agents.
Addresses the 'knowledge utilization problem' where LLMs may possess relevant user data but fail to act upon it.
Aims to differentiate between models that fail to remember information versus those that remember but fail to apply it contextually.

stories.title: Bridging the Question-Answer Gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings
stories.author: Aleksandar Tošić
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core limitation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems: the style mismatch between user queries and retrieved document content.
It proposes a method involving 'Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings' to improve alignment between the query and the retrieved context.
The research aims to mitigate the computational overhead associated with existing runtime solutions like HyDE, suggesting a more efficient approach to RAG improvement.

stories.title: Long-Running AI Agents Accumulate Context Debt
stories.author: vincent_tuan
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Context Debt' in long-running AI agents.
This debt arises as agents accumulate information from various sources (e.g., finance, CRM) over time.
The concept is illustrated using an agent preparing a monthly operating review.

stories.title: Gartner Says 40% of Apps Will Have AI Agents by December. Here's the Plumbing Nobody Puts on the Slide.
stories.author: mickyarun
bullet_points: Gartner predicts a significant adoption rate, stating 40% of enterprise apps will feature AI agents by December.
The article promises to delve into the underlying technical infrastructure ('the plumbing') required for this AI agent integration.
The source is Dev.to, suggesting the content is aimed at a developer audience interested in implementation details.
